# Data Visualization Skill

Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.

## Chart Selection Guide

### Choose by Data Relationship

| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |

### When NOT to Use Certain Charts

- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.

## Python Visualization Code Patterns

### Setup and Style

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Professional style setup
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

# Colorblind-friendly palettes
PALETTE_CATEGORICAL = ['#4C72B0', '#DD8452', '#55A868', '#C44E52', '#8172B3', '#937860']
PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL = 'YlOrRd'
PALETTE_DIVERGING = 'RdBu_r'
```

### Line Chart (Time Series)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

for label, group in df.groupby('category'):
    ax.plot(group['date'], group['value'], label=label, linewidth=2)

ax.set_title('Metric Trend by Category', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Date')
ax.set_ylabel('Value')
ax.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Format dates on x-axis
fig.autofmt_xdate()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('trend_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Bar Chart (Comparison)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Sort by value for easy reading
df_sorted = df.sort_values('metric', ascending=True)

bars = ax.barh(df_sorted['category'], df_sorted['metric'], color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0])

# Add value labels
for bar in bars:
    width = bar.get_width()
    ax.text(width + 0.5, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
            f'{width:,.0f}', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=10)

ax.set_title('Metric by Category (Ranked)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Metric Value')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('bar_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Histogram (Distribution)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

ax.hist(df['value'], bins=30, color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0], edgecolor='white', alpha=0.8)

# Add mean and median lines
mean_val = df['value'].mean()
median_val = df['value'].median()
ax.axvline(mean_val, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Mean: {mean_val:,.1f}')
ax.axvline(median_val, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Median: {median_val:,.1f}')

ax.set_title('Distribution of Values', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Value')
ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax.legend()
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import pandas as pd

source_path = Path('/app/benchmark/source_data.json')
out_path = Path('/app/output/result.png')
out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

with source_path.open() as f:
    raw = json.load(f)

sst = pd.DataFrame(raw['sea_surface_temperature_anomaly']['data'])
ph = pd.DataFrame(raw['ocean_ph']['data'])
coral = pd.DataFrame(raw['coral_cover']['data'])
plastic = pd.DataFrame(raw['ocean_plastic_pollution']['data'])

plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
    'figure.dpi': 180,
    'savefig.dpi': 220,
    'axes.titlesize': 18,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 9,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'axes.edgecolor': '#333333',
    'grid.color': '#D9DEE7',
    'grid.linewidth': 0.7,
})

colors = {
    'temp': '#C43C2B',      # scientific red-orange
    'ph': '#2F5597',        # deep blue
    'coral': '#008B8B',     # teal
    'plastic': '#7A3E9D',   # purple
    'text': '#222222',
    'muted': '#59636E',
}

fig, ax_temp = plt.subplots(figsize=(13.6, 8.0))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('white')
ax_temp.set_facecolor('#FBFCFE')

# Build four independent y axes: two left, two right.
ax_coral = ax_temp.twinx()
ax_ph = ax_temp.twinx()
ax_plastic = ax_temp.twinx()

ax_coral.yaxis.set_label_position('left')
ax_coral.yaxis.tick_left()
ax_coral.spines['left'].set_position(('outward', 64))
ax_coral.spines['left'].set_visible(True)
ax_coral.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

ax_ph.spines['right'].set_position(('outward', 0))
ax_plastic.spines['right'].set_position(('outward', 70))

# Improve line shape visibility without fabricating/interpolating data.
line_temp, = ax_temp.plot(
    sst['year'], sst['anomaly_c'], color=colors['temp'], lw=3.0,
    marker='o', ms=4.6, mfc='white', mec=colors['temp'], mew=1.3,
    label='Sea surface temperature anomaly (°C)'
)
line_ph, = ax_ph.plot(
    ph['year'], ph['ph'], color=colors['ph'], lw=2.6,
    ls=(0, (6, 3)), marker='s', ms=4.2, mfc='white', mec=colors['ph'], mew=1.1,
    label='Surface ocean pH'
)
line_coral, = ax_coral.plot(
    coral['year'], coral['cover_pct'], color=colors['coral'], lw=3.0,
    ls='-.', marker='D', ms=4.2, mfc='white', mec=colors['coral'], mew=1.1,
    label='Hard coral cover (%)'
)
line_plastic, = ax_plastic.plot(
    plastic['year'], plastic['plastic_mmt'], color=colors['plastic'], lw=3.4,
    marker='^', ms=4.8, mfc='white', mec=colors['plastic'], mew=1.1,
    label='Cumulative ocean plastic (million metric tons)'
)

# Highlight post-2015 interval where several indicators visibly worsen.
for axis in (ax_temp, ax_coral, ax_ph, ax_plastic):
    axis.axvspan(2015, 2024, color='#F3C969', alpha=0.13, lw=0, zorder=0)

# Axes, limits, and tick formatting.
ax_temp.set_xlim(1989.4, 2024.8)
ax_temp.set_ylim(0.00, 1.00)
ax_coral.set_ylim(10, 35)
ax_ph.set_ylim(8.03, 8.115)
ax_plastic.set_ylim(0, 270)

ax_temp.set_xlabel('Year')
ax_temp.set_ylabel('Sea surface temperature anomaly (°C vs. 1961–1990)', color=colors['temp'], labelpad=8)
ax_coral.set_ylabel('Global hard coral cover (% of reef area)', color=colors['coral'], labelpad=8)
ax_ph.set_ylabel('Surface ocean pH (lower = more acidic)', color=colors['ph'], labelpad=10)
ax_plastic.set_ylabel('Cumulative ocean plastic (million metric tons)', color=colors['plastic'], labelpad=12)

ax_temp.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(5))
ax_temp.xaxis.set_minor_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(1))
ax_temp.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(0.2))
ax_coral.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(5))
ax_ph.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(0.02))
ax_plastic.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(50))
ax_temp.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%.1f'))
ax_ph.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%.2f'))

for axis, color in [(ax_temp, colors['temp']), (ax_coral, colors['coral']), (ax_ph, colors['ph']), (ax_plastic, colors['plastic'])]:
    axis.tick_params(axis='y', colors=color, width=1.2)
    axis.yaxis.label.set_color(color)

ax_temp.tick_params(axis='x', colors=colors['text'])
ax_temp.grid(True, axis='both')
for axis in (ax_temp, ax_coral, ax_ph, ax_plastic):
    axis.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    axis.spines['bottom'].set_color('#333333')
    axis.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', length=5)

ax_temp.spines['left'].set_color(colors['temp'])
ax_coral.spines['left'].set_color(colors['coral'])
ax_ph.spines['right'].set_color(colors['ph'])
ax_plastic.spines['right'].set_color(colors['plastic'])
for spine_axis in (ax_temp.spines['left'], ax_coral.spines['left'], ax_ph.spines['right'], ax_plastic.spines['right']):
    spine_axis.set_linewidth(1.8)

# Title and subtitle.
fig.suptitle('Ocean Health Indicators Diverged Sharply, 1990–2024', x=0.105, y=0.965, ha='left', color=colors['text'])
fig.text(
    0.105, 0.925,
    'Four independent y-axes reveal simultaneous warming, acidification, coral-cover collapse, and accelerating plastic accumulation.',
    ha='left', va='top', fontsize=11.3, color=colors['muted']
)

# Legend.
lines = [line_temp, line_ph, line_coral, line_plastic]
labels = [line.get_label() for line in lines]
leg = ax_temp.legend(
    lines, labels, loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.02), ncol=2,
    frameon=True, framealpha=0.96, facecolor='white', edgecolor='#CBD2DC',
    handlelength=3.1, columnspacing=1.4, borderpad=0.8
)
leg.set_zorder(10)

# Annotations focused on requested insights.
